date.as_written: saṃvan saptadaśe śate badhur ddaśe varṣenduṣaśūklādvādaśī guro(!)

notes: 'saṃvan saptadaśe śate badhur ddaśe varṣe' means 'in the 17th century of the era (the 1700s), in the year …-daśa'. 'badhur ddaśe' is corrupt. Reading it as caturdaśe gives 1714, but other readings (e.g. vidhu = 1 → 1711) are possible. The era is not named; VS is assumed (Devanagari script, North Indian formula), which gives about 1657/58 CE. The month 'induṣa' (from 'varṣenduṣa') is probably corrupt, perhaps for pauṣa. 'upādevajīnena' is unclear. It could be a haplography for upā[dhyāya]-devajī-[sū]nunā ('son of Upādhyāya Devajī'), which is the reading used here. Alternatively the title upādhyāya may belong to the scribe, or Devajī may be a co-scribe. The scribe's name follows the catalogue (Mohanajīka); -jī is an honorific, so the base name may be Mohana. The lines 'ālohannamīnīpothī | ḍhānovamaḍīmītākī | rādhīyasarasīño hī' look like a corrupt Hindi/Braj verse, possibly an owner's or reader's jotting ('pothī' = book). No person can be read from them with confidence.
